import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io
from matplotlib.ticker import StrMethodFormatter

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set plotting style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", rc={"axes.edgecolor": ".8", "grid.linestyle": "--"})

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the bubble chart
# We encode 5 variables: year (x), price (y), brand (color), megapixels (size), body_type (marker style)
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='model_year',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='brand',
    size='megapixels',
    style='body_type',
    sizes=(200, 2500),  # Control the range of bubble sizes for better differentiation
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.5,
    ax=ax
)

# Add annotations for each point for more context
for i in range(df.shape[0]):
    row = df.iloc[i]
    ax.text(
        row['model_year'],
        row['price_usd'] + 150,  # Offset text vertically
        f"{row['sensor_type']}\n{row['weight_grams']}g",
        ha='center',
        va='bottom',
        fontsize=9,
        fontweight='medium',
        color='#333333'
    )

# --- Polish the visualization ---

# Set Title and Labels
ax.set_title('Camera Market Snapshot: Price vs. Release Year', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold', pad=25)
ax.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Format axis ticks
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(StrMethodFormatter('${x:,.0f}'))
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FormatStrFormatter('%d'))
plt.xticks(rotation=0)
plt.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)

# Adjust legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate the legends for clarity
brand_legend = plt.legend(handles[1:4], labels[1:4], title='Brand', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', fontsize=11, title_fontsize=13)
ax.add_artist(brand_legend) # Add the first legend back
size_legend = plt.legend(handles[4:7], labels[4:7], title='Megapixels', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.75), loc='upper left', fontsize=11, title_fontsize=13)
ax.add_artist(size_legend)
style_legend = plt.legend(handles[7:], labels[7:], title='Body Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.45), loc='upper left', fontsize=11, title_fontsize=13)

# Adjust plot limits to give space
ax.set_xlim(df['model_year'].min() - 2, df['model_year'].max() + 2)
ax.set_ylim(0, df['price_usd'].max() + 500)

# Final layout adjustment and save
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for legends
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
